results.title: We tell you when we cancel a price increase - Autoresearch - Autoresearch
highlights:
2. 01:00 UTC

### We tell you when we cancel a price increase

You say to your agent

> “Is the H100 price increase that you announced still on?”

If we cancel a price increase that we announced, the dashboard shows a notice that says so. Each organization that got the email about the increase gets a second email that cancels it. The email includes the text of the first one. See Rates.

...

## October 13, 2026

1. 20:00 UTC

### We tell you about a price increase before it takes effect

You say to your agent

> “Is the price of an H100 going to change soon?”

A price increase now always comes at least 24 hours before it takes effect, and we tell you about it. An increase is a higher list price, or a smaller Friday, weekend, or batch job discount.

When we schedule an increase, the dashboard shows a notice until a few days after it takes effect. The admins and billing members of each organization that used that type in the last 90 days get an email.

Your agent sees it too. Until the increase takes effect, `create_node` and `get_node` carry it in `rate.upcoming_increase`, and `submit_job` carries it in `upcoming_increase`. The field gives the time it takes effect, the new list rate per GPU and per node, and the new discounts. A running node also gets a `price_change` event on `/v1/events`. See Rates.

...

## October 8, 2026

1. 07:00 UTC

### The H100 price is now $5.04 per GPU-hour

On October 8 at 00:00 Pacific time, the H100 list price changed from $3.96 to $5.04 per GPU-hour. Per GPU-minute, the price changed from $0.066 to $0.084. A whole 8-GPU node now costs $40.32 per hour.

The new price applies to each minute that we bill from that time. This includes the minutes of nodes and jobs that were already running. Minutes before that time bill at the old price.

The discounts did not change, and they now apply to the new list price. Friday hours are 33% off, and Saturday and Sunday hours are 20% off, on the Pacific calendar. Batch jobs are 25% off the list price. The docs show the rates.

We did not tell you about this change before it took effect. We are sorry for the late notice. If you have a question about your bill, send it to us on the contact page.

results.title: Your GPU agent needs a price limit
highlights:
Rent vs buy economics · 2026-10-21

# Your GPU agent needs a price limit

SF Compute now exposes upcoming price increases to agents. For local-AI builders, the useful hedge is a workload that can move when the rental math changes.

...

Moving work requires a budget policy and a reproducible environment.

## The rental rate enters the control loop

On October 13, 2026, SF Compute’s Autoresearch added at least 24 hours of advance notice for price increases, including machine-readable notices for agents. Its October 8 H100 increase had arrived without advance warning: $3.96 became $5.04 per GPU-hour, including on running nodes. The company apologized. The dated changelog records both events.

The interesting development is the response. A rental agent can now see an upcoming increase through `rate.upcoming_increase` on node calls. That creates an opportunity to make price part of scheduling. It does not automatically enforce your budget; your own policy still has to decide what happens next.

...

Consider an illustrative evaluation requiring 100 H100 GPU-hours, all billed at the undiscounted rate. The compute bill rises from $396 to $504: $108 more for identical rented time, or 27.3%. A $500 compute budget previously bought about 126.3 GPU-hours; now it buys 99.2. These are calculations from the published rates, not measurements of model performance.

...

The rates documentation also describes calendar discounts: an interactive node can cross into cheaper Friday or weekend minutes, with days defined on the US Pacific calendar. The calendar and upcoming rate are exposed in responses. But a running node can still be repriced when the list price changes. Read the current billing rules; a quoted launch rate is insufficient protection.

...

One documentation wrinkle deserves care: the October 8 changelog says the increase applied to running jobs, while the current rates section says a job keeps its starting rate. That leaves historical versus current batch treatment unclear. The running-node rule is explicit; confirm batch treatment before relying on a price lock.

...

- Autoresearch changelog — October 8 and 13, 2026
- Autoresearch rates and billing documentation — checked October 21

results.title: SF Compute enables programmable GPU compute markets with physical settlement — Digest AI
highlights:
# SF Compute enables programmable GPU compute markets with physical settlement

SF Compute, led by CEO Evan Conrad, is building a programmable marketplace for GPU compute that goes beyond simple spot pricing. The company treats GPU capacity like a commodity, using physical settlement – actually delivering the hardware resources rather than a cash‑only contract – and matching orders with detailed constraints such as interruption tolerance, storage backup, and specific GPU…

## Key points

- SF Compute has placed about 5% of its GPU capacity on a programmable order book, achieving high liquidity for that slice.
- The firm uses physical settlement, delivering actual GPU compute and matching constraints such as interruption tolerance, storage backup, and GPU generation.
- Customers can lease compute from an hour up to three years; spot B300 rates are $5‑$6/hr, while resale inference can earn $25‑$40/hr.

Only about 5% of SF Compute’s total GPU capacity is currently on its order book, but that slice enjoys high liquidity. Customers can buy compute for as short as an hour or lock in capacity for up to three years. Spot prices for B300 GPUs run about $5‑$6 per hour, while reselling the same capacity for inference can generate $25‑$40 per hour, giving the firm an average $25 profit per $100 of capacity sold back.

results.title: Platts to launch US GPU Compute Prices, Nov. 23 | S&P Global
highlights:
Platts to launch US GPU Compute Prices, Nov. 23 | S&P Global 

 November 05, 2026

# Platts to launch US GPU Compute Prices, Nov. 23

Platts, part of S&P Global Energy, will launch US GPU Compute prices, effective Nov. 23, 2026.

Daily on-demand and interruptible prices will cover four NVIDIA chips: the NVIDIA H100, H200, B200 and B300 chips. Prices will be published in US dollars per GPU-hour and US dollars per million tokens of output, based on prices and availability at 1:30 pm CT.

COVERAGE

The assessments reflect the market value of available NVIDIA GPU compute capacity delivered through qualifying virtualized infrastructure services in the US by providers and marketplaces. The new assessments will capture an evolving segment of the compute market, where growing availability of dedicated GPU capacity and increasingly standardized service offerings have supported greater price transparency. The assessments will provide standardized price references for accessing GPU compute capacity in the US, adding further granularity to Platts coverage of the infrastructure supporting artificial intelligence workloads.

METHODOLOGY

Each GPU price will be a simple average of the prices of available GPUs for each chip and service type. Platts will review the prices for outliers and will automatically exclude any prices greater than 2 median absolute deviations from the median.

Platts may review the suitability of the current methodology and consider adopting a volume-weighted average approach once sufficient trade data has been collected. Platts encourages market participants to report trade data to ComputePricing@spglobal.com (PriceGroup@spglobal.com) for this purpose.

results.title: Evan Conrad: Magkakaroon ng pagkakaroon ng problema ang karamihan sa mga AI startup sa pag-access sa GPU capacity sa loob ng 6 na buwan | KuCoin
highlights: Ayon sa Mars Finance, noong Oktubre 22, ipinahayag ni Evan Conrad ang artikulong "The end of startups" na may pamagat na "The coming credit crunch." Si Evan Conrad: Sa loob ng susunod na anim na buwan, karamihan sa AI startups ay hindi makakabili ng computing power; ang buong mundo ay nasa full capacity na, at upang makakuha ng capacity, kailangan ng pag-sign ng bagong cluster—hindi na kaya ng mga entidad na hindi kwalipikado bilang investment-grade na makakuha ng online capacity. Ayon kay Evan Conrad, ang mga startup ay hindi investment-grade, kaya hinihingi na silang magbigay ng mas malaking advance payment; nakita niya ang mga kontrata na nangangailangan ng 100% advance payment dahil sa pag-iwas ng mga lender at cloud providers sa karagdagang credit risk. Kanyang sinabi na ang mga investment-grade tenant ay limitado, at ang kanilang credit rating ay bumaba dahil sa paggamit ng leverage at pagbebenta sa mga non-investment-grade token buyer, na tinatawag niyang credit bottleneck. Inaasahan niya na ang mga investment-grade GPU buyer ay lalabas na hihingi na ang mga token buyer ay investment-grade din o magbigay ng malaking down payment. Sa artikulo, binigyang halimbawa na sa oras ng pagsulat, maaaring bilhin ang B300 sa $6 bawat oras, at ibenta ang inference sa halos $30 bawat oras. Inaasahan niya na tataas ang presyo ng GPU at bumababa ang gross margin sa inference layer, at mas mahirap para sa mga customer na may mas mababang credit rating na makakuha ng token. Ibinigay niya ang ideya na gawing collateral ng mga lender ang GPU clusters, at sinabi niya na ang physical delivery forward market para sa computing power, SF Compute, ay maaaring gamitin ng mga lender bilang collateral ang GPU hours sa kanilang liquid ledger, kaysa mag-asa lamang sa isang serbisyo provider.

results.title: Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal
highlights:
Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

Image: GPUJournal price record — read on lambda.ai/pricing

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

results.title: RunPod Secure Cloud GPU Rates Rise: H100 $3.99, B200 $7.99
results.author: TSN Newsroom
highlights:
RunPod Secure Cloud GPU Rates Rise: H100 $3.99, B200 $7.99

# RunPod’s Secure Cloud GPU Rates Have Risen: H100 SXM Now $3.99 an Hour, B200 $7.99, a Tracker Reports

October 10, 2026

Illustration.

A GPU price tracker, GPU Economy, says RunPod raised 12 of its 29 on-demand Secure Cloud GPU rates on 8 October 2026 [1]. RunPod’s pricing page now shows the higher prices [2]. RunPod made no announcement that we could find, so the timing and the old prices rest on the tracker.

## The new rates

RunPod sells two tiers, Secure Cloud and Community Cloud; on its listings the Community rates are lower. Prices are in US dollars per GPU per hour, on demand, meaning pay as you go. GPU Economy reports [1]:

| GPU | Before | Now | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $3.49 | $3.99 | +14.3% |
| H200 | $4.59 | $5.29 | +15.3% |
| B200 | $6.79 | $7.99 | +17.7% |
| B300 | $7.89 | $8.99 | +13.9% |

The H100, H200, B200 and B300 are Nvidia data-centre chips used to train and run AI models. The tracker says the 12 rises came “between our reads of October 8, 2026 at 15:41 and 16:41 UTC”, which is 16:41 and 17:41 in London. It also computes that one H100 SXM running for a 730-hour month went from $2,547.70 to $2,912.70.

## What did not change

The tracker says “None of the 35 Community Cloud on-demand rates changed in the same read”: the H100 SXM there stayed at $2.69 and the B200 at $5.98 [1].

## What RunPod’s page shows

RunPod’s pricing page lists $3.99/hr for the H100 SXM, $7.99/hr for the B200, $5.29/hr for the H200 and $8.99/hr for the B300 [2]. But the page is labelled “Updated September 27, 2026”, which does not match the tracker’s 8 October timing. The page’s hidden structured data, the code search engines read, still lists the old Secure Cloud prices, such as $3.49 for the H100 SXM [2]. The tracker says it read RunPod’s public API, and that on 9 October the page’s own markup still carried $3.49 [1]. That fits what we see.

## What this does not show

- A RunPod announcement. We found none, and no reason for the rises.
- When RunPod made the change. The tracker reads hourly and gives a one-hour window.
- Other providers’ prices. This covers RunPod only.
- Every region or product. Serverless and cluster pricing are not covered.

results.title: The H100 got more expensive · Three Phase. Potentia Intelligence.
results.author: Jose Mir
highlights:
### One Big Thing · Phase 3 · Compute

What happened: Nebius raised on-demand GPU prices on October 1, its second hike in about three months. Independent trackers show the same direction across the market.

Why it matters: The bear case on AI infrastructure assumed GPUs lose value fast. Rental rates are the cleanest test of that assumption, and so far the test is failing.

By the numbers:

- Nebius list price for an H100 went from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour; B300 from $7.85 to $9.50.
- The Ornn H100 index settled at $3.17 on October 23, up about 4% in a month.

results.title: The Price of a GPU-Hour Is Now Set by Memory, Not Compute | AIChieve
results.author: Jorge Fernandez Ilufi
highlights:
Cloud provider Nebius raised its hourly rate for an Nvidia H100 chip from $3.85 to $4.50 on October 1, 2026, while pushing the newer B200 to $8.50. 

Cloud provider Nebius raised its hourly rate for an Nvidia H100 chip from $3.85 to $4.50 on October 1, 2026, while pushing the newer B200 to $8.50 [3]. The chips did not get faster, but their memory now costs much more. Two days prior, TrendForce raised its 2027 forecast for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) to a 121% jump over this year’s prices [1].

...

- 121% — HBM price jump: TrendForce expects the blended price of high-bandwidth memory to rise 121% next year due to tight supply and a shift to the newest HBM4 grade [1].
- 17% to 21% — Nebius rate hike: The cloud provider raised H100 rates to $4.50, H200 to $5.40, B200 to $8.50, and B300 to $9.50 per GPU-hour on October 1, 2026 [3].
- $8.55 vs $14.24 — B200 spread: An independent tracker puts the median on-demand B200 at $8.55 an hour at dedicated GPU clouds and $14.24 at large hyperscalers [5].
- 10% to 15% — DRAM contracts: TrendForce expects standard DRAM contract prices to climb another 10% to 15% in the fourth quarter [2].

...

What strikes me is that the price of the newest chip relies entirely on how much memory it holds, not how much math it does. A September index tracking rental rates put the B200 at $8.01 an hour [4]. It reported the chip now costs 21% more per unit of compute than the older H100 [4].
